nodes.text: Where the book stands, the saves and the wins, what is at risk, and the expansion plays that are landing.
Dana Whitfield, Head of Customer Success  ·  6 October 2026
a name next to every red account
Twenty-six new, eight churned, all eight under fifty seats.
Health score above 70; usage and support both trending up.
Mostly renewals inside ninety days with a champion change.
Sixteen accounts, $1.1M in annual revenue, each with a named plan.
One tile per account, largest first. Light dot: moved up a tier this quarter. Dark dot: moved down.
Score 40 to 69, or a renewal inside 90 days
Score under 40, or a champion gone
22 accounts moved up a tier and 9 moved down. 26 new logos, 8 churned, all eight under fifty seats.
the five biggest reds are on page six
Red in July after a champion left. New champion onboarded in two weeks; renewed for three years in September.
Blocked on a security review for four months. A named engineer cleared it in nine days.
Usage had halved. A workflow rebuild with their team doubled it back and added two departments.
the other nineteen are in the appendix
The week our champion left, Fernwood called us before we had worked out who to call.
renewed for three years in September
Where we need help, and by when
The four motions that are landing
A live customer walks a neighbouring team through their setup. Closed nine expansions this way.
At 80% of seats, the account manager books the review before the customer asks.
Twice a year for every account over $100K. Every expansion this quarter followed one.
Partners introduce their other customers. Four expansions, all in the first meeting.
all thirteen followed a business review
Coverage moves to pods of three, the sixteen red accounts each get a named owner, and the focus list is on the wall.
